paths.description: Mobile portal homepage: primary search, navigation, content feed, on-load overlays, preference adaptation, security, performance, and memory.
Search-results archetype and primary search journey, using a representative Daum query.
Public detail/content archetype reached from the homepage feed; checked metadata, structured data, reading layout, and mobile reflow.
Interactive content-menu editor archetype; checked controls, keyboard exposure, live feedback, and compact layout.
Low-relevance search query plus error-document responses used to inspect system state and recovery.

findings.summary: Motion continues when reduced motion is requested.
findings.evidence: The reduced-motion probe matched prefers-reduced-motion: reduce but found a 1,400 ms fade animation still running and no prefers-reduced-motion CSS rules.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a prefers-reduced-motion: reduce override that removes non-essential rolling/fade animation and disables auto-advance.

findings.summary: Some dark-theme text remains below WCAG contrast minimums.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured repeated 14 px metadata at 4.36:1 and blue labels at 3.75:1 against #2c2e33; the high-contrast capture did not expose a distinct higher-contrast theme.
findings.suggestedFix: Raise dark-theme token contrast to at least 4.5:1 and add prefers-contrast/forced-colors adaptations for essential UI.

findings.summary: Major state and route changes are abrupt.
findings.evidence: The CSS/DOM probe found no view-transition usage while the homepage exposes many dynamic category tabs and separate settings/search routes.
findings.suggestedFix: Progressively enhance category and route changes with same-document/cross-document View Transitions, with reduced-motion handling.

findings.summary: The 14,746 px feed has no scroll-state-aware orientation aid.
findings.evidence: The homepage layout is 14,746 px tall, while CSS inspection found no scroll-state container behavior or progress affordance and the navigation is not retained in long scrolled states.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep key section navigation available and add a lightweight scroll-state/progress affordance using CSS where supported.

findings.summary: An app-promotion modal obscures the main content on arrival.
findings.evidence: Both light and dark first-viewport screenshots show a large centered “다음 커뮤니티 오픈!” app promotion covering headlines and feed content.
findings.suggestedFix: Do not open the promotion before user intent; use a non-blocking inline placement or delayed, frequency-capped prompt with obvious dismiss.

findings.summary: The on-load modal is not exposed through a semantic top-layer primitive.
findings.evidence: The screenshot shows a modal, but the DOM probe found zero dialog, popover, or role=dialog elements, so modal semantics and platform dismissal are absent.
findings.suggestedFix: Use <dialog> for the modal flow, invoke showModal(), label it, manage initial focus, and support Escape/platform close.

findings.summary: The representative article template renders as a desktop-width page on a 390 px phone.
findings.evidence: Article layout reported inner/scroll width 1,184 px and 794 px horizontal overflow; the screenshot clips the headline and lead image far beyond the right edge.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove the desktop minimum width, keep width=device-width effective, and use fluid/intrinsic sizing so the article reflows at 320–390 px.

findings.summary: Reusable feed components depend on global layout rather than container-aware adaptation.
findings.evidence: CSS inspection across the dense, reused homepage card/tab surface found no @container rules or container-type declarations.
findings.suggestedFix: Introduce container queries for cards, tab strips, and embedded modules that appear at multiple widths; keep viewport queries as fallback.

findings.summary: Zoom and several touch interactions are constrained.
findings.evidence: The homepage viewport declares user-scalable=no and maximum-scale=1.0; Lighthouse also found overlapping/insufficient safe target space in the main tab strip.
findings.suggestedFix: Allow pinch zoom, remove maximum-scale/user-scalable restrictions, and provide at least 24x24 CSS px target size and spacing.

findings.summary: The homepage misses the Core Web Vitals loading and stability bars.
findings.evidence: Mobile Lighthouse measured LCP 14.4 s, CLS 0.159, and TBT 240 ms (performance 0.46); the independent layout observer measured CLS 0.260.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile the LCP dependency chain, prioritize the actual LCP resource, reserve dynamic regions, and defer non-critical feed/ad work.

findings.summary: Late content causes substantial layout movement.
findings.evidence: The layout observer recorded four shifts totaling CLS 0.260, including two roughly 0.09–0.10 shifts after 8.7 s; 94 of 100 images lacked both dimensions.
findings.suggestedFix: Reserve exact aspect-ratio space for images, ads, and asynchronous feed modules before content arrives.

findings.summary: Main-thread work delays interactivity.
findings.evidence: The trace found two long tasks, longest 153 ms and 114 ms TBT; Lighthouse attributed 5.1 s to main-thread work and 1.5 s to script bootup.
findings.suggestedFix: Break long tasks, schedule non-essential work by priority, and delay ad/feed initialization until after the critical experience.

findings.summary: The critical delivery chain is large and render-blocking.
findings.evidence: HAR captured 195 requests and 3.07 MB; parser-inserted CSS and a synchronous head analytics script were high-priority candidates. Lighthouse estimated 1.23 s render-blocking savings and 1.76 MB cache savings.
findings.suggestedFix: Inline only critical CSS, defer non-critical styles/scripts, remove synchronous analytics from the head, and set effective cache headers.

findings.summary: The page ships substantial unused and legacy code.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 698 KiB unused JavaScript, 80 KiB unused CSS, and 132 KiB legacy JavaScript; HAR shows 1.24 MB across 22 scripts.
findings.suggestedFix: Use route/component-level code splitting, conditionally load feed/ad features, and stop serving unnecessary legacy bundles to modern browsers.

findings.summary: Several controls and embedded frames lack complete accessible semantics.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found an unnamed Daum-logo link, ad iframes without titles, and tab roles without required tablist parents; the image audit reported 80 images without alt.
findings.suggestedFix: Name icon links, title or hide decorative frames, implement complete tablist/tab/tabpanel relationships, and give meaningful images accurate alt text.

findings.summary: Text contrast fails in dark mode.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse identified repeated 14 px metadata at 4.36:1 and blue labels at 3.75:1, both below 4.5:1.
findings.suggestedFix: Adjust dark-theme color tokens and verify all foreground/background combinations with automated and visual checks.

findings.summary: ARIA tab structure is incomplete.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reported multiple role=tab links whose required role=tablist parent is missing. Native focus was visible, but incomplete relationships impair assistive navigation.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a conforming tab pattern with tablist, tab, aria-controls, tabpanel, roving tabindex, and keyboard arrow behavior.

findings.summary: The article cannot be read comfortably at the audited phone width.
findings.evidence: At 390 px, the 1,184 px article canvas clips the headline, metadata, and image; users must pan horizontally.
findings.suggestedFix: Make article typography and media fluid, cap line length, and test reflow at 320 CSS px and 400% zoom.

findings.summary: The homepage prevents zoom and the article fails mobile reflow.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed meta-viewport because user-scalable=no disables zoom; article layout has 794 px overflow at a 390 px visual viewport.
findings.suggestedFix: Permit user scaling and ensure all templates reflow without two-dimensional scrolling at narrow/zoomed conditions.

findings.summary: A shipped fallback image returns 404.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse console evidence and HAR both recorded a 404 for noimg_224_150.gif.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish the fallback asset or update/remove the stale URL, then ensure expected network failures are handled without console noise.

findings.summary: Image markup is frequently unsized and sometimes uses incorrect aspect ratios.
findings.evidence: Image audit found 94/100 images without both dimensions; Lighthouse showed thumbnails declared width="100%" with a 0.57 displayed ratio versus 1.80 intrinsic ratio.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide numeric width/height attributes that match source aspect ratio and use CSS width:100%;height:auto plus aspect-ratio where appropriate.

findings.summary: Deprecated APIs and platform hygiene issues remain.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found an unload listener, deprecated Topics API usage, BFCache blockers, broken/missing source maps, and inspector issues.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace unload with pagehide/visibility handling, remove deprecated Topics calls, restore source maps, and make BFCache-compatible lifecycle choices.

findings.summary: The article has no meta description.
findings.evidence: The article recon returned a descriptive title but an empty meta description, while the homepage had both.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate a concise, content-specific description for every article/detail page.

findings.summary: Many navigation controls are implemented as non-crawlable links.
findings.evidence: Recon found app/search controls with href="javascript:;" and category tabs with href="#none"; these are neither semantic buttons nor crawlable destinations.
findings.suggestedFix: Use <button> for in-page actions and real href URLs for navigable categories, progressively enhancing tab behavior.

findings.summary: Homepage indexing signals are incomplete.
findings.evidence: The homepage probe found no canonical URL; both /robots.txt and /sitemap.xml returned branded 404 documents.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish intentional robots.txt and sitemap signals and add a self-referencing canonical for the public homepage.

findings.summary: The portal homepage lacks structured WebSite metadata.
findings.evidence: The homepage has four Open Graph tags but zero JSON-LD blocks; the article template does provide DiscussionForumPosting JSON-LD and rich OG tags.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate WebSite/Organization JSON-LD, including SearchAction only if it matches the visible search behavior.

findings.summary: Transport is HTTPS, but CSP and cookie protections are incomplete.
findings.evidence: Headers evidence shows no CSP or X-Content-Type-Options. Cookie evidence found four non-Secure cookies and all six with SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a nonce/hash-based CSP, add nosniff, and mark all cookies Secure with the narrowest workable SameSite and HttpOnly posture.

findings.summary: The homepage has a broad tracking and advertising footprint.
findings.evidence: Tracker capture found 20 third-party origins and known DoubleClick/Google ad trackers; HAR recorded 190 third-party requests and 2.66 MB attributed outside the exact m.daum.net origin.
findings.suggestedFix: Inventory third parties, remove low-value trackers, gate non-essential advertising/analytics by consent and context, and batch/minimise events.

findings.summary: Several browser-enforced defenses are absent.
findings.evidence: The main response has HSTS and X-Frame-Options but lacks CSP, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, and X-Content-Type-Options.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a restrictive Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy, add nosniff, and enforce framing through CSP frame-ancestors alongside legacy X-Frame-Options.

findings.summary: Most homepage content disappears without JavaScript.
findings.evidence: Discoverability measured only 7% raw/rendered content overlap; the no-JS screenshot preserves header chrome but leaves the feed blank although raw HTML is 2.5 MB.
findings.suggestedFix: Server-render meaningful feed links and text, then hydrate enhancements; keep primary search and category navigation functional without JavaScript.

findings.summary: Language is declared, but layout CSS is not writing-mode resilient.
findings.evidence: The DOM correctly declares lang="ko", while CSS inspection found no logical inline/block properties across the representative homepage styles.
findings.suggestedFix: Retain the correct lang attribute and replace physical left/right spacing/positioning with logical properties in reusable layout code.

findings.summary: The app promotion uses a nagging, content-blocking acquisition pattern.
findings.evidence: The promotion appears immediately above the portal content and makes the app CTA dominant; dismissal exists but the interruption precedes any expressed intent.
findings.suggestedFix: Move acquisition messaging into content flow, frequency-cap it, preserve a prominent dismiss choice, and never obscure the user’s requested content.

findings.summary: Image delivery wastes bytes and misses responsive optimization.
findings.evidence: Image audit found 79 below-fold images without lazy loading, 31 oversized images, 70 without srcset, and 27 legacy-format images; Lighthouse estimated 422 KiB image savings.
findings.suggestedFix: Lazy-load below-fold media, provide responsive srcset/sizes, serve AVIF/WebP where useful, and right-size decorative assets.

findings.summary: Substantial advertising and feed work runs during initial load.
findings.evidence: The page performs 195 requests, including 20 ad API requests and 15 analytics-origin requests, while Lighthouse reports 5.1 s of main-thread work.
findings.suggestedFix: Defer and batch background analytics/ad work, stop fetching offscreen modules until needed, and cancel work when hidden.

findings.summary: Third-party and media cost is disproportionate in the first load.
findings.evidence: HAR totals 3.07 MB, with 2.66 MB and 190 requests classified outside the exact homepage origin; images and scripts each transfer about 1.25 MB.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a per-template request/byte budget, lazy-load below-fold media, and require third-party scripts to justify measurable user value.

findings.summary: Repeated category switching retains substantially more heap in the post-interaction snapshot.
findings.evidence: After ten representative tab activations, heap self-size rose from 46.27 MB to 58.75 MB (+27%), objects from 55,184 to 88,938, and closures from 39,133 to 59,177. Separate fresh sessions and dynamic feed variance lower certainty, but the retained delta warrants investigation.
findings.suggestedFix: Reproduce in one controlled session with baseline/target/final snapshots, force GC between stages, and trace retained tab data/listeners before fixing the owning component.

findings.summary: The initial JavaScript heap graph is large for a mobile portal entry state.
findings.evidence: The baseline heap summary contains 687,161 nodes and 46.27 MB self size before deliberate interaction; the page also renders a 14,746 px feed and ships 22 scripts.
findings.suggestedFix: Virtualize/defer far-below-fold modules, unload inactive category state, and set a measured mobile heap budget.

taskList.title: Fix mobile reflow and restore zoom across every template
